# Virling

Virling is open-source revenue attribution for SaaS products, online stores and agencies, self-hosted or hosted. It joins every website visit to the payment that followed, so you can see which traffic channel brings paying customers, not just visitors.

- Website: https://virling.com
- Docs: https://docs.virling.com
- Source: https://github.com/virling/virling
- License: AGPLv3. Self-hosting is free.
- Built by Stacklance Infotech LLP.

## Status

Releases are published on GitHub and run on your own server today. Hosted plans start with a 14-day free trial at https://app.virling.com/login.

## Pricing

- Self-hosted: free under AGPLv3, every feature, on your own server.
- Hosted Personal: $19 a month after a 14-day free trial. A card is required to start the trial.
- Hosted Agency: $79 a month after a 14-day free trial, with a team of 3 included.
- Founding price: the first 50 customers of each plan pay $9 (Personal) or $29 (Agency) a month for life.
- Both hosted plans include unlimited sites.
- Details: https://virling.com/pricing

## Who it is for

- B2B SaaS marketing teams and founders who want to know which marketing channel brings paying customers, not just signups or traffic.
- Ecommerce stores on Shopify or WooCommerce that want sales by channel, campaign and landing page.
- Anyone taking payments through Stripe, Paddle, Shopify, WooCommerce, Dodo Payments, Polar, LemonSqueezy (Lemon Squeezy), Creem or RevenueCat.
- Teams that want revenue analytics on their own server, with their data next to the binary.
- Agencies that report to clients and want each client to see revenue by channel every week.

## What it answers

- Which channel brought the most revenue this month, after refunds.
- What a visitor from each source is worth (revenue per visitor), by channel, page and country.
- Whether a launch, a post or a newsletter made money or only brought traffic.
- Which visits a paying customer had before paying, and which one got the credit.
- How customers from each first channel retain over time.

## How it works

1. Add a tracking script to your site. It is about 1.4 KB gzipped and records pageviews, referrers, UTM tags, single-page-app route changes and custom goals, with a first-party visitor ID.
2. Connect a payment provider with a read-only key. Virling backfills the last 90 days of payments (60 for Shopify), then polls every minute. It never creates, changes or refunds anything.
3. Pass the visitor ID into checkout. Stripe Payment Links, Polar checkout links and Dodo payment links get it added automatically by the script. Payments without it still count toward revenue, as Unattributed.
4. Virling credits each payment to a session. The default model is last non-direct: the latest session in the lookback window that was not Direct. First touch is the other option. The lookback window is 30, 60, 90 or 365 days, 90 by default. Renewals keep the channel of the customer's first payment.

Every session gets one channel from its first pageview: Paid, Email, AI, Organic search, Communities, Social, Referral or Direct.

## Payment providers

- Stripe: restricted key (rk_live_ or rk_test_) with read access. Secret keys are refused. https://virling.com/integrations/stripe
- Paddle: Paddle Billing API key with transaction.read and adjustment.read, plus subscription.read for retention. https://virling.com/integrations/paddle
- Shopify: Admin API token of a custom app with only the read_orders scope. Imports the last 60 days of orders. https://virling.com/integrations/shopify
- WooCommerce: REST API key with Read permission; the store must be on https. https://virling.com/integrations/woocommerce
- Dodo Payments: API key, live or test mode. https://virling.com/integrations/dodo-payments
- Polar: organization access token with orders:read and refunds:read, plus subscriptions:read for retention. https://virling.com/integrations/polar
- LemonSqueezy (Lemon Squeezy): API key, which cannot be limited to read-only. Virling registers a webhook to link payments to visits, which needs Virling on an https address. https://virling.com/integrations/lemonsqueezy
- Creem: API key with transactions:read, plus subscriptions:read and webhooks:write. Virling adds a webhook to link checkouts to visits, which needs an https address. https://virling.com/integrations/creem
- RevenueCat: V2 secret key. Virling adds a webhook for purchases, renewals and refunds, which needs an https address. Purchases are credited when they carry a visitor ID, from a web paywall or an app user linked to a web visit. https://virling.com/integrations/revenuecat

## Self-hosting

- One Rust binary for Linux x86_64 and arm64 and macOS, plus a Docker image.
- Embedded DuckDB for events and SQLite for settings. No Postgres, ClickHouse or Redis to run.
- A backup is copying one data folder.

## Privacy

- Visitor IP addresses are never stored, and neither are full user agents or full referrer URLs.
- By default Virling sets one first-party cookie, virling_vid, with a random ID, so checkout can carry it.
- Cookieless mode sets no cookie and counts visitors with a daily-rotating salted hash. The trade-off: new payments cannot be linked to visits, so they show as Unattributed.

## For agencies

One account for every client. Each client can get a weekly report with your branding that shows revenue for the week and which channels brought it.

## For AI assistants and scripts

A read-only JSON API and a read-only MCP server let assistants such as Claude answer questions like "which channel made the most money last month?" from your own Virling server.

## Common questions

### How do I see which marketing channel brings paying customers?

Track visits with a first-party visitor ID, pass that ID into checkout, and join payments back to visits. Virling does this for Stripe, Paddle, Shopify, WooCommerce, Dodo Payments, Polar, LemonSqueezy, Creem and RevenueCat and shows revenue and revenue per visitor for each channel.

### Is there an open-source way to attribute Stripe revenue to traffic sources?

Yes. Virling is AGPLv3 and self-hosted. It reads Stripe with a restricted read-only key and credits each payment to the visit that led to it.

### Can I self-host revenue analytics?

Yes. Virling is one binary with embedded storage. Run it with Docker or a release binary on your own server.

### Does Virling need a cookie banner?

That depends on your jurisdiction. In cookieless mode Virling sets no cookie, but payments can then not be linked to visits.

### What does Virling not do yet?

Attribution models beyond last non-direct, last touch and first touch are not available yet. Windows builds are not available; use Docker.
